description.narrative: This initiative provides support to the Ministry of Planning, Development and Reform for public sector reforms and innovation for improved performance and service delivery, citizen’s satisfaction and reducing multi-dimensional poverty

sector.narrative: Structural transformation, including green, inclusive and digital transitions

condition.narrative: Social and environmental sustainability will be enhanced through application of the UNDP Social and Environmental Standards (http://www.undp.org/ses) and related Accountability Mechanism (http://www.undp.org/secu-srm).
UNDP as the Implementing Partner will comply with the policies, procedures and practices of the United Nations Security Management System (UNSMS.)

comment.narrative: 1.1: Scale 2 (very partially functional) (No performance-based management system exists in government institutions. Performance reports (ACR/PERs) are used but they are not effectively tied to performance) 1.2: Scale 2 (very partial capacity) (Ministries have limited capacity in place to effectively manage performance-centered reforms) 1.3: Scale 2 (very partially) (Only limited digital mechanisms for government transparency, accountability and responsiveness exist such as e-filing in Establishment Division) 1.4: Scale 1 (not at all) (Public service delivery is very conventional and the perception of government’s public service delivery is poor and there is little motivation or incentive to improve or recognition of innovation) 2.1: Scale 2 (to a small extent) (Research exists, such as the NCGR report and previous Pay Commission reports, but are rarely used to inform the way of work) 2.2: Scale 2 (very partially) (There is general agreement that the civil service needs improvement but there is considerable skepticism about the reform effort, lack of clarity on what is to be done, and wide difference about how to go about it) 2.3: Scale 1 (No study) (There is a general consensus that public sector service delivery need to be improved. However, there is not much information on evidence of the type of governance reforms needed to achieve this) 4.1: Scale 2 (to a small extent) (Insufficient human resource capacities, systems, procedures and MOPDR hamper its performance) 4.2: Scale 2 (to a small extent) (There is general support but incomplete understanding of reforms as shown through media reports and social media feedback) 4.3: Scale 3 (two of the three types) (Research is created but only has limited dissemination, use and influence on policy)

The case studies are in progress and will be completed in 2021, hence an achievement rating of 2. 1.3: 2- (Very Partially)-.Supporting Federal Government (e.g. Prime Minister Office, Establishment Division, Federal Public Services Commission, Auditor General of Pakistan, Accountant General Pakistan Revenues) to install wide-scale restructuring and e-governance measures to improve transparency, accountability and responsiveness. The project is conducting an all-encompassing digital readiness assessment of the Ministry of Information Technology & Telecommunication (MoITT) and its key attached organizations: National Information technology Board, IGNITE, and National Telecommunication Corporation. This assessment will gauge organizational digital readiness in three categories: a) infrastructure maturity b) business process continuity c) digital readiness of employees. 1.4:0 (The project had planned to organize Innovation Awards / Fund / Policy and National Consultation on Governance reforms / models. However, the activity could not be implemented on account of government priorities.) 2.1: 4- The project actively contributed actionable research towards implementation of reforms. The Terms of Reference for conducting studies on Civil Service / Service Delivery Reforms (Recruitment, Trainings, Job Descriptions, Performance Management, Tenure Protection, and Compensation were prepared and shared with the donor and the government.
Anti-corruption / integrity module for training of probationary officers at the Civil Services Academy (CSA) introduced. The objective of this module is to inculcate a sense of integrity and accountability into the mindset of new officers right at the start of their careers 2.2: 3- (Partially)-The project actively liaised with all key stakeholder groups (including the Task Forces on Civil Service Reforms and Austerity, CCIR and the MoPDSI) to facilitate a consultation-based reform effort.

The activity could not be implemented due to change in government priorities. However, the project actively engaged with the PMs Task Forces on Civil Service Reforms and Austerity, CCIR and the MoPDSI which are taking a lead in civil service reform debate in Pakistan.

However, extensive consultations held with CCIR, MoPDSI and the Task Forces to support the government’s reform agenda.

1.1: Scale 3 [The project provided support to the Office of Special Assistant to Prime Minister on Establishment for implementation of Performance Contracts signed by the Prime Minister with Federal ministries and divisions. Strategic communications support provided to PMO for development of communications strategy, and organizing Performance Contracts Awards Ceremony, along with development of communications collateral. Strengthened capacity of Prime Minister’s Delivery Unit by identifying areas and sectors which are constantly failing to perform at the required levels, and proposing concrete remedial measures for enhancing performance]. 1.2: Scale 3 [Provided technical assistance to all ministries and divisions (41) through a team of support consultants aimed at capacity development for implementation of performance contracts]. 1.3: Scale 3 [Digitization of performance agreements through National Information Technology Board (NITB) was carried out. The end product was an enhanced Performance Agreements Portal which interfaces with the users (ministries) and supports the Peer Review Committee (PRC), responsible for the final clearance on the agreements. Provided technical and operational support to Pakistan Customs for development and launch of an Online Complaint Portal for facilitating traders, especially the young entrepreneurs, in hassle-free lodging of complaints – thus promoting ease of doing business and improving governance outcomes by enabling digital interventions]. 1.4: Scale 4 Partially for both 2.1: 4 [Commissioned an ‘Executive Recruitment in Public Sector Organizations’ study as a diagnostic exercise to provide evidence and reasons behind delays in the recruitment process for top-level vacancies in public sector organizations in Pakistan. The study provides data on 68 public sector organizations; analyses laws governing the hiring process, and multiple challenges faced by public sector organizations in hiring for senior positions. Based on this review, a set of recommendations grounded in international case studies and best practices followed by public and private sectors were proposed to the government. Subsequent to the above-mentioned study, the project was requested to support the MoPDSI in development of a Recruitment Manual for Executive Level Hiring encompassing a review of the legal framework governing the recruitment processes of public sector organizations, identify hinderances in fast-track recruitment and propose concrete ways to improve the recruitment strategy through amendments in the relevant rules. The study will help the government in streamlining recruitment processes for senior positions on contract basis, and fast-tracking recruitment through documenting HR policies, procedures, and rules]. The project also conducted a study to comprehensively review the civil service salary structures in Pakistan. The study titled ‘Civil Service Compensation: Incentives, Dissatisfaction and Costs’ was conducted in partnership with Pakistan Institute of Development Economics (PIDE). A comprehensive review and updation of the ‘Manual for Development Projects’ was carried out in response to a request by MoPDSI. The last edition of the Manual was prepared in 1997, followed by the ‘Guidelines for Project Management’ published in 2008. During a span of over 12 years, numerous changes were introduced in the processes and procedures of development projects, which warranted fresh documentation]. 2.2:0 – [Activity cancelled due to change in government priorities.] 2.3: 2 [Completed two rounds of an extensive three-phase survey to measure citizens’ satisfaction with public service delivery in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and Punjab. The survey covers access and acceptability of public services including WASH, health, education and citizens’ engagement and awareness, with a sample of 27,720 households.] 3.1:1- No result 3.2:2- No result 3.3:3- No result 4.1: scale 3 [ Strengthened MoPDSI’s capacity as a think-tank to Government of Pakistan through development of a comprehensive Technical Assistance (TA) plan to help target high impact areas of MoPDSI to ensure a stronger integration and internalization of reforms. The TA plan addresses four priority areas including M&E capabilities, policy evaluation function, development of strategic documents and business process refinement]. 4.2: 0 [Activity cancelled due to change in government priorities.] 4.3: 2 [The project created an extensive knowledge and research base which is supporting innovation and reforms in governance and public service delivery at the MoPDSI during the previous years.
